candidate.scope: Grouped poster component illustration of cDNA barcoding, unequal amplification, sequencing and barcode-based RNA abundance estimation. All four printed targets are retained. The drawn material route is supported for Digital RNA; applicability to the other grouped names is assessed separately against their own papers. The visible SUPeR-seq, UMI Method, MARS-Seq and chemical legend are neighboring context with no connection to this row. No equivalence or historical relationship among the four names is asserted. Primary evidence resolves the other three printed targets to distinct implementations that do not implement this particular fixed-input route. Their supported architecture differences are stated in method_scopes and corrections. Compact, separate sequencing/readout interfaces record the paper-supported interpretations for these named targets; upstream preparation is retained only as input history, not reconstructed as additional workflows. These interfaces are distinguished from the original drawn route and are not evidence of a new depicted alternative branch. cDNA1 and cDNA2 are two independent illustrated molecular families under shared captions, not evidence of separate sample compartments or a pooling step.

evidence.locator: Full text [b00025], Allele specific library generation, sequencing and frequency determination
evidence.quote: In the initial step, the region containing genetic variation (SNPs or deletions) is amplified by PCR using allele-specific primers containing overhangs shown in Figure 1B and listed in Table S1.

FREQ-Seq utilizes two rounds of PCR that take advantage of the inclusion of a small amount of a long, bridging primer that can be produced and re-generated in-house at low cost in order to introduce sample-specific bar-codes ( Figure 1 ).

This results in production of DNA fragment pools already compatible with the Illumina single-end read flow cell, obviating all subsequent library preparation steps (e.g., shearing, adapter ligation, column selection, etc.).
The resulting products are then pooled and sequenced en masse on a Illumina HiSeq or Genome Analyzer flow cell.

evidence.quote: Here we report RNAtag-Seq, a method for generating a single RNA-seq library containing large numbers of RNA samples that are barcoded and pooled before library construction (Online Methods, Fig. 1 and Supplementary Protocol).

Barcoding in RNAtag-Seq is achieved through direct ligation of adaptors to RNA, enabling strand-specific, quantitative sequencing of full-length transcripts in diverse prokaryotic and eukaryotic species at a quality highly comparable to that of the well-established dUTP method7 for single-sample library construction (Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2 and Supplementary Table 1).

evidence.locator: Full text [b00016], Online Methods: Generation and sequencing of cDNA libraries
evidence.quote: These pools of barcoded RNAs were converted to Illumina cDNA libraries in three key steps: (i) reverse transcription of the RNA using a primer designed to the constant region of the barcoded adaptor; (ii) degradation of the RNA and ligation of a second adaptor to the single-stranded cDNA; (iii) PCR amplification using primers that target the constant regions of the 3′ and 5′ ligated adaptors and contain the full sequence of the Illumina sequencing adaptors (Fig. 1).
